docs.title: Overview
docs.text: ### Quantitative technical analysis, cross-sectional alpha research and vectorized backtesting in Polars  **Transparent mathematical expressions. Institutional factor analytics and risk modeling. An intuitive dual `.anta` / `.ta` interface. Polars clarity with Rust-accelerated performance.**

docs.title: What is polars-anta?
docs.text:
polars-anta (Alpha & Numerical Technical Analysis) is an open-source quantitative finance library for technical analysis, market microstructure estimation, cross-sectional factor engineering, and vectorized backtesting in Python and Polars.

Designed for quantitative researchers, algorithmic traders, data scientists, and students, polars-anta implements technical indicators, statistical regressions, formulaic alpha primitives, and portfolio evaluation tools directly as Polars Expressions (pl.Expr)—combining readable, inspectable mathematical formulas with Polars' multi-threaded Rust execution engine.

A Simple Core Idea:

Quantitative Pipeline = OHLCV Data + Native Polars Expressions (.anta / .ta) + Cross-Sectional Alpha + Vectorized Backtest

docs.title: Why polars-anta?
docs.text:
• End-to-end quantitative coverage — move seamlessly from raw OHLCV validation and technical indicators to cross-sectional factor neutralization, IC/quantile evaluation, and vectorized backtesting.
  • Transparent implementations — inspect clean, closed-form algebraic Polars expressions rather than opaque C/Cython binaries.
  • Rust-accelerated performance — up to 112.4x faster than Pandas on 1,000,000 rows via multi-threaded Rust query execution and zero-copy stride tricks.
  • Zero C compilation — installs in seconds via pip install polars-anta across Windows, macOS, and Linux with no external C headers or MSVC/GCC toolchains.
  • Learn by example — explore ready-to-run Python scripts, 1-click Google Colab notebooks, and modular API reference guides.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text: pip install polars-anta

docs.title: 2. Compute Indicators & Alpha Factors
docs.text:
import polars as pl
import polars_anta as pa  # Registers .anta and .ta namespaces

df = pl.read_parquet("market_data.parquet")

features = df.with_columns(
    pl.col("close").anta.ema(20).over("symbol").alias("ema_20"),
    pl.col("close").anta.rsi(14).over("symbol").alias("rsi_14"),
    pl.col("close").anta.linear_regression_slope(14).over("symbol").alias("ols_slope"),
    pl.col("close").anta.bollinger_bands(20, 2.0).over("symbol").alias("bb"),
).unnest("bb")

docs.title: 3. Run a 1-Line Vectorized Backtest
docs.text:
bt = (
    df.anta.ema(12, alias="ema_12")
    .anta.ema(26, alias="ema_26")
    .anta.backtest(
        entries=pl.col("ema_12").anta.crosses_above("ema_26"),
        exits=pl.col("ema_12").anta.crosses_below("ema_26"),
        fee_rate=0.0005,
        initial_capital=100_000.0,
    )
)
print(bt.report())

docs.title: Architecture & Design Principles
docs.text: polars-anta is engineered around three fundamental architectural pillars:

docs.title: 1. Zero-C Dependency & Zero GIL Bottleneck
docs.text:
Existing technical analysis packages force quant researchers into an unpleasant dilemma: - TA-Lib: Written in C. Fast, but notoriously difficult to compile on Windows/macOS, crashes frequently on ABI mismatches, and lacks native DataFrame integration. - pandas-ta: Pure Python. Easy to install, but suffers from Python's Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), resulting in slow single-threaded loops on large datasets.

polars-anta circumvents this entirely: - Zero C Compilation: Pure Polars expressions ensure installation always works out of the box (pip install polars-anta). - Native Rust Execution: Polars pushes expression execution into its multi-threaded Rust analytical engine, bypassing Python's GIL. - Dual Namespace Ergonomics: Supports both .anta and .ta on any Polars expression without performance cost.

docs.title: 2. Apache Arrow Memory Format & Zero-Copy Pipelines
docs.text:
Traditional Python pipelines waste significant CPU cycles converting data back and forth between NumPy arrays, Python lists, and C buffers.

In polars-anta: - Data remains in contiguous Arrow memory blocks. - Intermediate indicator steps share memory through Arrow buffers without memory replication. - Streaming operations process chunked batches without out-of-memory (OOM) crashes on gigabyte-scale datasets.

docs.title: 3. Parallel Multi-Asset Windowing via .over()
docs.text:
In quantitative finance, features must be computed across a universe of assets (e.g. 500 S&P 500 stocks or thousands of crypto pairs).

In Pandas: 

# Slow: Single-threaded Python loop over groups
df.groupby("ticker").apply(lambda g: g["close"].rolling(20).mean())

In Polars: 

# Blazingly fast: Polars parallelizes groups across all CPU threads in Rust
df.with_columns(pl.col("close").anta.sma(20).over("ticker"))

By leveraging Polars' window context .over("ticker"), calculations for all tickers run concurrently across CPU cores with zero extra code.

docs.title: Benchmarks & Performance Analysis
docs.text: To evaluate real-world performance, polars-anta provides an automated benchmarking suite (benchmarks/benchmark_speed.py) comparing execution speeds against Pandas / NumPy baselines across 1,000,000 rows.

docs.title: Benchmark Results
docs.text: Operation / Indicator Dataset Scale Pandas (s) polars-anta (s) Measured Speedup Linear Regression Slope 1,000,000 bars 1.8018 s 0.0154 s 116.8x Faster Multi-Asset RSI 500 tickers x 2k bars 0.4560 s 0.0610 s 7.5x Faster Multi-Asset SMA 500 tickers x 2k bars 0.1229 s 0.0176 s 7.0x Faster Z-Score Normalization 1,000,000 bars 0.0378 s 0.0182 s 2.1x Faster Exponential Moving Average 1,000,000 bars 0.0093 s 0.0058 s 1.6x Faster Simple Moving Average 1,000,000 bars 0.0187 s 0.0097 s 1.9x Faster

docs.title: 1. Vectorized Linear Regression Decomposition
docs.text:
Traditional packages compute rolling linear regression by taking 1,000,000 windows and repeatedly solving \(y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 t\) with NumPy dot products.

polars-anta decomposes the OLS closed-form equation into Linearly Weighted Moving Average (WMA) and Simple Moving Average (SMA):

\[\beta_1 = \frac{6}{N - 1} (\text{WMA} - \text{SMA})\]

Because WMA and SMA execute in SIMD-vectorized Rust kernels, the rolling regression evaluates in 0.015 seconds instead of 1.80 seconds—over 116x faster!

docs.title: 2. Multi-Threaded Partitioning (.over())
docs.text: When processing multiple tickers, Polars automatically partitions data and distributes computation across all physical and logical CPU cores in Rust. Pandas .groupby().apply(), by contrast, iterates sequentially in a single Python thread.

docs.title: How to Reproduce
docs.text:
Run the benchmark script directly on your own machine:

pip install -e .[benchmark]
python benchmarks/benchmark_speed.py

docs.title: Guidelines for New Indicators
docs.text:
When adding a new indicator:

  1. Pure Expression First: Implement using pl.Expr wherever possible. Avoid Python loops over rows.
  2. Support String or Expr: Use parse_expr from polars_anta.core so users can pass either column names ("close") or existing expressions (pl.col("close")).
  3. Register on Dual Namespaces: Indicators added to TechnicalAnalysisExpr in polars_anta/namespace.py are automatically available under both .anta and .ta.
  4. Multi-Asset Compatibility: Ensure the indicator executes without errors inside .over("ticker").
  5. Structured Outputs: If the indicator produces multiple values (like bands or oscillators with signals), return a typed pl.Struct.
  6. Comprehensive Tests: Add test cases to the appropriate file in tests/. Verify test coverage remains above 90%: 
    pytest -v
  7. Code Quality: Ensure linter and formatter pass without errors: 
    ruff check .
ruff format --check .

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install polars-anta using pip:

pip install polars-anta

Requirements: - Python >= 3.10 - Polars >= 1.0.0

No C compiler or MSVC / GCC tools are needed.

docs.title: Core Paradigm: Expression-First
docs.text:
In Polars, computations are expressed as expressions (pl.Expr) rather than eager array modifications. This allows Polars to optimize queries, combine multiple operations into a single execution pass, and parallelize calculations across all CPU threads.

Importing polars_anta automatically attaches both .anta and .ta namespaces to Polars expressions:

import polars as pl
import polars_anta

docs.title: 1. Basic Calculation
docs.text:
Calculate indicators using .anta.<indicator>() (or .ta.<indicator>()) directly on columns:

df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "open": [10.0, 10.5, 11.0, 10.8, 11.2],
        "high": [10.8, 11.2, 11.5, 11.1, 11.8],
        "low": [9.8, 10.2, 10.7, 10.5, 10.9],
        "close": [10.5, 11.0, 10.8, 11.2, 11.5],
        "volume": [1000, 1200, 950, 1100, 1500],
    }
)

result = df.with_columns(
    pl.col("close").anta.sma(3).alias("sma_3"),
    pl.col("close").anta.rsi(3).alias("rsi_3"),
    pl.col("close").anta.zscore(3).alias("zscore_3"),
)
print(result)

docs.title: 2. Multi-Component Struct Indicators
docs.text:
Indicators that output multiple components (like MACD, Bollinger Bands, Stochastic, Ichimoku) return a typed pl.Struct expression.

You can unpack all components into individual columns using .unnest():

# Compute Bollinger Bands
df_bands = df.with_columns(
    pl.col("close").anta.bollinger_bands(period=3, num_std=2.0).alias("bb")
).unnest("bb")

# Now columns `upper`, `middle`, `lower`, `bandwidth`, `percent_b` are directly available
print(df_bands.select(["close", "upper", "middle", "lower"]))

docs.title: 3. Functional Syntax
docs.text:
If you prefer functional import style, all indicators can also be imported directly from polars_anta:

from polars_anta import sma, rsi, bollinger_bands

result = df.with_columns(
    sma("close", period=3).alias("sma_3"),
    rsi("close", period=3).alias("rsi_3"),
    bollinger_bands("close", period=3).alias("bb"),
)

docs.title: 4. Fluent DataFrame & LazyFrame Chaining
docs.text:
In addition to expression-level calls, polars-anta provides direct DataFrame and LazyFrame chaining via .anta and .ta:

import polars as pl
import polars_anta

# Validate data, resample, and chain indicators directly:
features = (
    df.anta.validate_ohlcv()
    .anta.resample("15m", group_by="symbol")
    .anta.sma(20)
    .anta.rsi(14)
    .anta.macd(unnest=True)
    .anta.bollinger_bands(unnest=True)
)

# Or batch generate a complete feature suite:
all_features = df.anta.add_all(group_by="symbol")

docs.title: Parallel Multi-Asset Scaling with .over()
docs.text: A frequent challenge in quantitative backtesting and real-time scanning is computing indicators across an entire universe of tickers (e.g. all 500 S&P 500 stocks or thousands of crypto spot pairs).

docs.title: The Traditional Bottleneck (Pandas)
docs.text:
In Pandas, grouping operations execute sequentially in a single Python thread:

# Slow & serial (runs on 1 CPU core)
df["sma_20"] = df.groupby("ticker")["close"].transform(lambda x: x.rolling(20).mean())
df["rsi_14"] = df.groupby("ticker")["close"].apply(calculate_rsi)

For 500 tickers \(\times\) 2,000 bars (1,000,000 rows), this single-threaded approach takes seconds to execute and scales poorly.

docs.title: The Polars Advantage: Native Windowing
docs.text:
In Polars, any expression can be partitioned across groups using .over("ticker"):

import polars as pl
import polars_anta

# Fast & parallelized across all CPU cores in Rust
universe_with_indicators = universe_df.with_columns(
    [
        pl.col("close").anta.sma(20).over("ticker").alias("sma_20"),
        pl.col("close").anta.rsi(14).over("ticker").alias("rsi_14"),
        pl.col("close").anta.macd().over("ticker").alias("macd"),
        pl.col("close").anta.obv("volume").over("ticker").alias("obv"),
        pl.col("close").anta.zscore(20).over("ticker").alias("zscore_20"),
    ]
)

docs.title: Why it is faster:
docs.text:
1. Multi-Threaded Rayon Thread Pool: Polars automatically allocates separate tickers to separate worker threads.
  2. Zero Serialization: No Python function callback overhead per group.
  3. Cache Coherency: Data stays in Arrow chunked arrays, maximizing CPU L1/L2 cache hit rates.

docs.title: Multi-Timeframe Resampling & DataFrame API
docs.text:
In quantitative workflows, analysts and traders often ingest tick or 1-minute market data and need to resample it into higher-timeframe bars (e.g., 5-minute, 15-minute, 1-hour, 1-day) before calculating technical features.

polars-anta provides: 1. resample_ohlcv: High-performance, zero-copy OHLCV aggregation powered by Polars' group_by_dynamic. 2. validate_ohlcv: Instant structural integrity validation (High >= Low, non-negative prices, no out-of-order timestamps). 3. Fluent DataFrame & LazyFrame Namespaces: Direct method chaining via df.anta... or df.ta... (and lf.anta... or lf.ta...).

docs.title: Single Asset Resampling
docs.text:
import polars as pl
from polars_anta import resample_ohlcv

# Resample 1-minute bars to 1-hour bars:
df_1h = resample_ohlcv(df_1m, every="1h")

Under the hood, resample_ohlcv computes standard financial candle rules: - open: First open price in the window - high: Maximum high price in the window - low: Minimum low price in the window - close: Last close price in the window - volume: Sum of volume in the window (if present)

docs.title: Multi-Ticker Universe Resampling
docs.text:
When handling universe data containing hundreds or thousands of tickers:

# Resample multi-ticker data in parallel:
universe_1h = resample_ohlcv(
    universe_1m,
    every="1h",
    group_by="symbol",
    time_col="timestamp",
)

You can also pass multi-column groups, such as group_by=["exchange", "symbol"].

docs.title: Custom Column Names and Additional Aggregations
docs.text:
resampled = resample_ohlcv(
    df,
    every="15m",
    time_col="date_time",
    open_col="open_price",
    high_col="high_price",
    low_col="low_price",
    close_col="close_price",
    volume_col="turnover",
    additional_aggs=[
        pl.col("num_trades").sum().alias("trades_count"),
        pl.col("spread").mean().alias("avg_spread"),
    ],
)

docs.title: 2. OHLCV Data Validation
docs.text:
Before training machine learning models or deploying algorithmic strategies, validating data integrity is essential:

from polars_anta import validate_ohlcv

# 1. Strict mode (default): returns original df if valid, raises ValueError on error
clean_df = validate_ohlcv(df)

# 2. Multi-ticker validation:
clean_universe = validate_ohlcv(universe_df, group_by="symbol")

# 3. Report mode: returns structured diagnostics dictionary without raising
report = validate_ohlcv(df, return_report=True)
if not report["valid"]:
    print("Errors found:", report["errors"])
    print("Metrics:", report["metrics"])

Checks performed: - Schema types: price columns are numeric, timestamp is Date or Datetime. - Candle consistency: high >= low, high >= open, high >= close, low <= open, low <= close. - Values: prices and volume are non-negative. - Timestamps: detects null timestamps and out-of-order timestamps per group.

docs.title: 3. Fluent DataFrame & LazyFrame API (.anta and .ta)
docs.text: Both .anta and .ta namespaces are registered directly on pl.DataFrame and pl.LazyFrame.

docs.title: Method Chaining
docs.text:
import polars as pl
import polars_anta

df_features = (
    df.anta.validate_ohlcv()
    .anta.resample("15m", group_by="symbol")
    .anta.sma(period=20)
    .anta.ema(period=50)
    .anta.rsi(period=14)
    .anta.macd(unnest=True)
    .anta.bollinger_bands(period=20, unnest=True)
)

docs.title: Struct Unnesting & Prefixes
docs.text:
Multi-output indicators (MACD, Bollinger Bands, Stochastic, Supertrend, etc.) can be kept as a pl.Struct or expanded into individual columns with clear prefixes:

# Keep as struct column `bb`
df.anta.bollinger_bands(period=20, unnest=False)

# Unnest into `bb_upper`, `bb_middle`, `bb_lower`, `bb_bandwidth`, `bb_percent_b`
df.anta.bollinger_bands(period=20, unnest=True, prefix="bb_")

docs.title: Full Quant Suite in One Pass: .add_all()
docs.text:
Compute a comprehensive, standard set of technical indicators across trend, momentum, volatility, volume, and statistical alpha factors in a single parallelized pass:

# Generates SMA, EMA, ADX, SuperTrend, RSI, MACD, Stoch, Williams %R, CCI, ROC,
# ATR, Bollinger Bands, Keltner Channels, OBV, VWAP, CMF, MFI, ZScore, TS Rank
features_df = df.anta.add_all(group_by="symbol")

docs.title: LazyFrame Out-of-Core Execution
docs.text:
The DataFrame namespace works seamlessly on pl.LazyFrame, enabling streaming execution for datasets larger than available RAM:

lf_plan = (
    pl.scan_parquet("data/*.parquet")
    .anta.resample("1h", group_by="ticker")
    .anta.sma(20)
    .anta.rsi(14)
    .anta.add_all(group_by="ticker")
)

# Executes in multi-threaded Rust query engine
result = lf_plan.collect()

docs.title: API Reference & Indicator Catalog
docs.text:
polars-anta provides high-performance technical indicators, cross-sectional alpha primitives, statistical regressions, factor evaluation tools, and vectorized backtesting utilities, organized into seven specialized modules:

Domain / Module Key Functionality API Reference 1. Trend & Overlays (polars_anta.trend) Moving averages (sma, ema, hma, kama, t3, alma), heikin_ashi, supertrend, ichimoku, adx, psar, ssl_channel, pivot_points Trend API → 2. Momentum Oscillators (polars_anta.momentum) rsi, macd, ppo, stochastic, stoch_rsi, squeeze_momentum, stc, tsi, fisher_transform, cci, williams_r, kst Momentum API → 3. Volatility & Channels (polars_anta.volatility) atr, natr, bollinger_bands, keltner_channels, donchian_channels, chandelier_exit, parkinson_volatility, garman_klass_volatility, ulcer_index Volatility API → 4. Volume & Money Flow (polars_anta.volume) vwap, vwap_bands, obv, cmf, mfi, adl, klinger, force_index, nvi, pvi, vpci, vr Volume API → 5. Quantitative Statistics (polars_anta.stats) zscore, percentile_rank, skewness, kurtosis, rolling_cov, rolling_corr, rolling_beta, rolling_alpha, closed-form OLS linear_regression_* Statistics API → 6. Alpha & Microstructure (polars_anta.alpha) cs_rank, cs_zscore, cs_winsorize, neutralize, amihud_illiquidity, roll_spread, corwin_schultz_spread, kyle_lambda, hurst_exponent, formulaic alphas (alpha_001–alpha_101) Alpha & Microstructure API → 7. Evaluation & Backtesting (polars_anta.evaluation, backtest) forward_returns, information_coefficient, ic_summary, quantile_analysis, factor_turnover, sharpe_ratio, sortino_ratio, calmar_ratio, max_drawdown, vectorized_backtest Evaluation & Backtest API →

docs.title: How polars-anta is Organized
docs.text:
The library separates data engineering, indicator & alpha expressions, factor evaluation, and vectorized backtesting into clean, inspectable modules:

polars_anta/
├── trend.py        # Moving averages, trend overlays, candlestick transforms & pivots
├── momentum.py     # Momentum oscillators, cycle detectors & divergence indicators
├── volatility.py   # OHLC volatility estimators, ATR stops & price channels
├── volume.py       # Volume-weighted price, money flow & accumulation metrics
├── stats.py        # Rolling moments, CAPM beta/alpha & closed-form OLS regression
├── alpha.py        # Cross-sectional factor ops, market microstructure & formulaic alphas
├── evaluation.py   # Alphalens-style IC/IR, quantile monotonicity & risk metrics
├── backtest.py     # Loop-free vectorized backtester, crossover signals & tearsheets
├── resample.py     # Multi-timeframe OHLCV resampling & schema/integrity validation
└── namespace.py    # Dual .anta and .ta registration on Expr, DataFrame & LazyFrame

docs.title: Three Ways to Invoke Any Function
docs.text:
Every indicator and primitive in polars-anta can be called through three interchangeable interfaces:

import polars as pl
import polars_anta as pa  # Registers .anta and .ta on Expr, DataFrame, and LazyFrame

# 1. Expression Namespace (.anta or .ta) — composable inside .select() / .with_columns()
df.with_columns(
    pl.col("close").anta.rsi(14).over("symbol").alias("rsi_14"),
    pl.col("close").ta.ema(20).over("symbol").alias("ema_20"),
)

# 2. DataFrame / LazyFrame Fluent Chaining — rapid end-to-end pipelines
df.anta.validate_ohlcv().anta.rsi(14).anta.macd(unnest=True).anta.backtest(
    entries=pl.col("rsi_14").anta.crosses_above(30),
    exits=pl.col("rsi_14").anta.crosses_below(70),
)

# 3. Direct Functional Import — explicit function calls
df.with_columns(pa.rsi("close", period=14).alias("rsi_14"))

docs.title: Alpha Factor & Microstructure Primitives
docs.text: Inspired by Kakushadze (2015, 101 Formulaic Alphas), WorldQuant, and modern quantitative factor investing, these building blocks allow quantitative analysts to compose complex multi-asset predictive alphas, market microstructure estimators, and portfolio weights natively in Polars expressions.

docs.title: cs_rank(expr, over=None, method="average", percentile=True)
docs.text: Cross-Sectional Rank (WorldQuant Alpha primitive rank(x)). Computes the rank of values across assets at each point in time. When percentile=True, scales the ranks between \(1/N\) and \(1.0\) (or \(0.0\) to \(1.0\)).

docs.title: cs_zscore(expr, over=None, clip_bound=None)
docs.text: Cross-Sectional Z-Score Standardization. Standardizes an alpha signal across the asset universe at each timestamp (\((x - \mu_t) / \sigma_t\)), with optional symmetric clipping into \([-\text{clip\_bound}, \text{clip\_bound}]\).

docs.title: cs_winsorize(expr, over=None, method="quantile", lower=0.01, upper=0.99, threshold=3.0)
docs.text: Cross-Sectional Winsorization (Outlier Clipping). Clips extreme cross-sectional outliers across the asset universe at each timestamp using empirical quantiles ("quantile"), standard deviation bounds ("zscore"), or Median Absolute Deviation ("mad").

docs.title: neutralize(expr, by, over=None, standardize=False)
docs.text: Group / Industry / Sector Neutralization (WorldQuant Alpha primitive indneutralize(x, g)). Demeans an alpha signal within categorical groups (e.g. industry, sector), ensuring the resulting portfolio is dollar-neutral with respect to that classification. When standardize=True, also divides by the group standard deviation to yield z-scores.

docs.title: ts_scale(expr, a=1.0, over=None)
docs.text: Scale Primitive (WorldQuant Alpha primitive scale(x, a)). Rescales values such that the sum of their absolute values equals \(a\): \(a \cdot x / \sum |x|\). Commonly used to size long/short portfolio positions with targeted gross leverage.

docs.title: ts_rank(close, period=10)
docs.text: Time-series rank. Computes the rank of the current element within the lookback window, scaled from 0.0 (lowest) to 1.0 (highest).

docs.title: ts_argmax(close, period=10)
docs.text: Number of bars ago the maximum price occurred in the lookback window (0 = today).

docs.title: ts_argmin(close, period=10)
docs.text: Number of bars ago the minimum price occurred in the lookback window.

docs.title: decay_linear(close, period=10)
docs.text: Linearly decayed moving average with weights \([1, 2, \dots, N]\). Essential building block for factor momentum decay.

docs.title: ts_delta(expr, period=1)
docs.text: Time-series Delta (WorldQuant Alpha primitive delta(x, d)): \(x_t - x_{t - d}\).

docs.title: ts_delay(expr, period=1)
docs.text: Time-series Delay / Lag (WorldQuant Alpha primitive delay(x, d)): \(x_{t - d}\).

docs.title: signed_power(expr, exponent=2.0)
docs.text: Signed Power (WorldQuant Alpha primitive signed_power(x, a)): \(\text{sign}(x) \cdot |x|^a\). Preserves direction while non-linearly expanding signal magnitudes.

docs.title: ts_min(expr, period=10)
docs.text: Rolling time-series minimum over lookback window (WorldQuant Alpha primitive ts_min(x, d)).

docs.title: ts_max(expr, period=10)
docs.text: Rolling time-series maximum over lookback window (WorldQuant Alpha primitive ts_max(x, d)).

docs.title: ts_sum(expr, period=10)
docs.text: Rolling time-series sum over lookback window (WorldQuant Alpha primitive ts_sum(x, d)).

docs.title: ts_std(expr, period=10)
docs.text: Rolling time-series standard deviation over lookback window (WorldQuant Alpha primitive ts_std(x, d)).

docs.title: ts_correlation(x, y, period=10)
docs.text: Rolling Pearson correlation between \(x\) and \(y\) over lookback window (WorldQuant Alpha primitive correlation(x, y, d)).

docs.title: ts_covariance(x, y, period=10)
docs.text: Rolling sample covariance between \(x\) and \(y\) over lookback window (WorldQuant Alpha primitive covariance(x, y, d)).

docs.title: ts_product(expr, period=10)
docs.text: Rolling time-series product \(\prod_{i=0}^{d-1} x_{t-i}\) over lookback window (WorldQuant Alpha primitive product(x, d)).

docs.title: ts_zscore(close, period=20)
docs.text: Time-series rolling Z-score: \((x - \text{mean}) / \text{std}\).

docs.title: returns_divergence(close, volume, period=14)
docs.text: Price vs Volume Returns Divergence: \(\text{ZScore}(R_{price}) - \text{ZScore}(R_{vol})\). Identifies divergence between price movement and volume backing.

docs.title: hl_ratio(high, low)
docs.text: Log intraday price expansion: \(\ln(\text{High} / \text{Low})\).

docs.title: co_ratio(close, open)
docs.text: Log intraday drift / conviction: \(\ln(\text{Close} / \text{Open})\).

docs.title: volume_weighted_momentum(close, volume, period=10)
docs.text:
Price momentum amplified or dampened by relative trading volume:

\[\text{ROC}(P, period) \times \frac{\text{Volume}}{\text{SMA}(\text{Volume}, period)}\]

docs.title: relative_spread(high, low, close)
docs.text: Normalized high-low spread relative to closing price: \((\text{High} - \text{Low}) / \text{Close}\).

docs.title: twap(high, low, close, period=20)
docs.text: Time-Weighted Average Price. Rolling mean of typical price \((H + L + C) / 3\).

docs.title: entropy(close, period=20, bins=5)
docs.text: Rolling Shannon Information Entropy of return distribution. Quantifies regime uncertainty: low entropy signifies strong directional trending, while high entropy indicates choppy market noise.

docs.title: fractal_dimension(high, low, period=20)
docs.text: Ehlers' Fractal Dimension (FRAMA component). Measures the fractal roughness of price motion bounded between \(1.0\) (smooth directional trend) and \(2.0\) (random noise).

docs.title: hurst_exponent(close, period=50)
docs.text: Rolling Hurst Exponent via Rescaled Range (R/S) analysis. Measures long-term memory: \(H > 0.5\) indicates persistent trending, \(H < 0.5\) indicates mean-reverting, and \(H \approx 0.5\) indicates random walk.

docs.title: amihud_illiquidity(close, volume, period=20, scale=1e6)
docs.text: Amihud (2002) Illiquidity Ratio. Measures price impact per unit of dollar trading volume over a rolling window: $\(\text{ILLIQ}_t = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \frac{|R_{t-k}|}{P_{t-k} \cdot V_{t-k}} \times \text{scale}\)$

docs.title: roll_spread(close, period=20)
docs.text: Roll (1984) Implicit Effective Bid-Ask Spread Estimator. Estimates proportional bid-ask bounce from first-order serial autocovariance of log price changes: $\(S_{\text{Roll}} = 2 \sqrt{\max(0, -\text{Cov}(\Delta \ln P_t, \Delta \ln P_{t-1}))}\)$

docs.title: corwin_schultz_spread(high, low, period=20)
docs.text: Corwin & Schultz (2012) High-Low Effective Bid-Ask Spread Estimator. Separates transient bid-ask bounce from true volatility using 1-bar and 2-bar High/Low log ranges without requiring L2 orderbook data.

docs.title: kyle_lambda(close, volume, period=20, scale=1e6)
docs.text: Kyle (1985) Price Impact Coefficient (\(\lambda\)). Estimates the rolling regression slope of price returns per unit of signed order flow (\(\text{sign}(R_t) \cdot V_t\)).

docs.title: 5. Canonical Formulaic Alphas (33 WorldQuant 101 Alphas)
docs.text:
polars-anta includes 33 pre-built institutional formulaic alphas from Zura Kakushadze (2016), 101 Formulaic Alphas (alpha_001 through alpha_030, alpha_041, alpha_054, and alpha_101). All formulaic alphas support both expression-level invocation and DataFrame/LazyFrame chaining (df.anta.alpha_012(group_by="symbol")).

Function Inputs Required Key Mechanism / Description alpha_001 – alpha_010 open, high, low, close, volume Volatility-conditional signed power rank, volume-price correlation reversals, open-VWAP divergence, and 5-day trend persistence alpha_011 – alpha_020 open, high, low, close, volume VWAP-close extrema, momentum-volume reversal (alpha_012), rank covariance (alpha_013–alpha_016), and high-breakout ranking alpha_021 – alpha_030 open, high, low, close, volume Bollinger/volume regime switches (alpha_021), 20-day high breakouts (alpha_023), volume-rank correlation (alpha_026), and 3-day sign momentum (alpha_030) alpha_041(high, low, close, volume) high, low, close, volume Geometric High-Low midpoint vs. VWAP: \(\sqrt{\text{High} \times \text{Low}} - \text{VWAP}\) alpha_054(open, high, low, close) open, high, low, close Intraday candlestick power ratio: \(-\frac{(\text{Low} - \text{Close}) \cdot \text{Open}^5}{(\text{Low} - \text{High}) \cdot \text{Close}^5 + 10^{-4}}\) alpha_101(open, high, low, close) open, high, low, close Normalized intraday body-to-range momentum: \(\frac{\text{Close} - \text{Open}}{(\text{High} - \text{Low}) + 10^{-4}}\)

docs.title: Factor Evaluation, Performance Metrics & Vectorized Backtesting
docs.text: polars-anta provides an institutional-grade suite for evaluating alpha factor predictive power (Alphalens-style Information Coefficient, ICIR, Quantile Monotonicity, Turnover) alongside scalar Strategy Performance & Risk Expressions and a loop-free Vectorized Backtesting Engine (df.anta.backtest()).

docs.title: forward_returns(df, close_col="close", periods=(1, 5, 10), group_by=None, prefix="fwd_ret_")
docs.text:
Computes multi-horizon forward returns \((P_{t+k} / P_t) - 1\) across single-asset or multi-asset (group_by="symbol") DataFrames and LazyFrames.

eval_df = df.anta.forward_returns(periods=(1, 5, 10), group_by="symbol")

docs.title: information_coefficient(df, factor_col, return_col, group_by=None, method="spearman")
docs.text: Computes the cross-sectional Rank IC (method="spearman", default) or Normal IC (method="pearson") time series between an alpha factor column and a forward return column at each timestamp (group_by="timestamp"). Returns an eager pl.DataFrame with [group_by, "ic", "n_obs"].

docs.title: ic_summary(df, factor_col, return_col, group_by=None, method="spearman")
docs.text:
Computes comprehensive summary statistics of a factor's Information Coefficient: - ic_mean: Mean cross-sectional IC - ic_std: Standard deviation of IC - icir: Information Ratio of IC (\(\text{IC}_{\text{mean}} / \text{IC}_{\text{std}}\)) - t_stat: Student's \(t\)-statistic testing \(\text{IC} \neq 0\) - hit_rate: Proportion of timestamps with \(\text{IC} > 0\) - n_periods: Number of cross-sectional periods evaluated

stats = eval_df.anta.ic_summary("alpha_012", "fwd_ret_1", group_by="timestamp")

docs.title: quantile_analysis(df, factor_col, return_col, quantiles=5, group_by=None, annualization=252.0)
docs.text: Partitions observations into \(Q\) cross-sectional factor quantiles (\(1 \dots Q\)) per timestamp and computes per-bucket performance metrics (count, mean_factor, mean_return, std_return, sharpe_ratio, win_rate, cumulative_return) to verify factor monotonicity.

docs.title: factor_turnover(df, factor_col, asset_col="ticker", time_col="timestamp", lag=1)
docs.text: Measures signal stability across time by computing cross-sectional rank autocorrelation (rank_autocorr) and L1 portfolio weight turnover (turnover) at each timestamp.

docs.title: 2. Strategy Performance & Risk Expressions (pl.Expr)
docs.text:
All performance metrics are implemented as native Polars expressions (pl.Expr) and can be used inside df.select(), df.group_by("symbol").agg(), or via .anta / .ta expression namespaces.

Function Signature Return Type Mathematical Definition drawdown_series(returns_or_equity, is_returns=True) pl.Expr (Series) Underwater percentage drawdown curve \((E_t - \max_{s \le t} E_s) / \max_{s \le t} E_s \le 0.0\) max_drawdown(returns_or_equity, is_returns=True) pl.Expr (Scalar) Worst peak-to-trough percentage decline \(\min_t \text{DD}_t\) sharpe_ratio(returns, risk_free_rate=0.0, annualization=252.0) pl.Expr (Scalar) Annualized Sharpe Ratio \(\frac{\mathbb{E}[r - r_f]}{\sigma(r - r_f)} \sqrt{N_{\text{ann}}}\) sortino_ratio(returns, risk_free_rate=0.0, annualization=252.0) pl.Expr (Scalar) Annualized Sortino Ratio using downside deviation \(\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[\min(0, r - r_f)^2]}\) calmar_ratio(returns, annualization=252.0) pl.Expr (Scalar) Annualized Return divided by \(\|\text{Max Drawdown}\|\) profit_factor(returns) pl.Expr (Scalar) Gross Profit divided by \(\|\text{Gross Loss}\|\) ($\sum r^+ / \sum win_rate(returns, include_zeros=False) pl.Expr (Scalar) Proportion of active periods with positive returns \(r_t > 0\)

docs.title: crosses_above(a, b, over=None) & crosses_below(a, b, over=None)
docs.text:
Returns a boolean Polars expression that evaluates to True on the exact bar where expression a crosses above (or below) expression or scalar threshold b.

entries = pl.col("ema_12").anta.crosses_above("ema_26")
rsi_oversold = pl.col("rsi_14").anta.crosses_above(30)

docs.title: signals_to_positions(entries, exits, short_entries=None, short_exits=None, over=None)
docs.text: Converts discrete boolean entry/exit triggers into a continuous position series in \(\{-1.0, 0.0, +1.0\}\) using Polars' native .forward_fill() state machine with zero Python loops.

docs.title: vectorized_backtest(df, ...) / df.anta.backtest(...)
docs.text:
Executes a single-asset or multi-asset vectorized backtest with automatic look-ahead protection (signal_lag=1), proportional fee & slippage deduction (turnover * (fee_rate + slippage_rate)), cross-sectional portfolio weight schemes ("raw", "dollar_neutral", "long_only", "equal_weight"), and Buy & Hold benchmark comparison.

bt = (
    df.anta.ema(12, alias="ema_12")
    .anta.ema(26, alias="ema_26")
    .anta.backtest(
        entries=pl.col("ema_12").anta.crosses_above("ema_26"),
        exits=pl.col("ema_12").anta.crosses_below("ema_26"),
        fee_rate=0.0005,
        slippage_rate=0.0002,
        initial_capital=100_000.0,
    )
)
print(bt.report())

docs.title: BacktestResult & compare_strategies(strategies)
docs.text:
• bt.data: Polars DataFrame containing position, turnover, asset_return, gross_return, cost, net_return, equity_curve, benchmark_equity, and drawdown.
  • bt.summary: Dictionary of 18 key performance and risk metrics.
  • bt.summary_df(transpose=False): Converts summary metrics into a Polars DataFrame.
  • bt.report(): Formatted human-readable tearsheet DataFrame with units ($, %, x).
  • pa.compare_strategies({"Strat A": bt_a, "Strat B": bt_b}): Side-by-side multi-strategy comparison table.

docs.title: Momentum Oscillators (21 Indicators)
docs.text: Momentum indicators measure the velocity, acceleration, and overbought/oversold extremes of price movements.

docs.title: rsi(close, period=14)
docs.text: Relative Strength Index using Wilder's smoothed moving averages. Oscillates between 0 and 100.

docs.title: macd(close, fast=12, slow=26, signal=9)
docs.text: Moving Average Convergence Divergence. Returns Struct: macd, signal, histogram.

docs.title: stochastic(high, low, close, k=14, d=3)
docs.text: Stochastic Oscillator. Returns Struct: %K, %D.

docs.title: stoch_rsi(close, rsi_period=14, stoch_period=14)
docs.text: Stochastic RSI. Applies the Stochastic formula to RSI values for heightened sensitivity. Returns Struct: %K, %D.

docs.title: williams_r(high, low, close, period=14)
docs.text: Williams %R. Reflects the level of close relative to the highest high over the lookback period.

docs.title: cci(high, low, close, period=20)
docs.text: Commodity Channel Index. Identifies cyclical turns by measuring deviations from statistical mean price.

docs.title: roc(close, period=10)
docs.text: Rate of Change. Measures percentage price change: \((P_t - P_{t-n}) / P_{t-n} \times 100\).

docs.title: awesome_oscillator(high, low, fast=5, slow=34)
docs.text: Bill Williams' Awesome Oscillator (AO). Difference between 5-period and 34-period SMAs of median price.

docs.title: tsi(close, long_period=25, short_period=13)
docs.text: True Strength Index. Double-smoothed momentum indicator that filters noise.

docs.title: cmo(close, period=14)
docs.text: Chande Momentum Oscillator. Calculates momentum on both up and down days, bounded between \(-100\) and \(+100\).

docs.title: ppo(close, fast=12, slow=26, signal=9)
docs.text: Percentage Price Oscillator. MACD expressed in percentage terms. Returns Struct: ppo, signal, histogram.

docs.title: coppock(close, wma_period=10, fast_roc=11, slow_roc=14)
docs.text: Coppock Curve. Long-term momentum oscillator designed for spotting major market bottoms.

docs.title: ultimate_oscillator(high, low, close, p1=7, p2=14, p3=28)
docs.text: Larry Williams' Ultimate Oscillator (UO). Combines momentum across three different timeframes.

docs.title: fisher_transform(high, low, period=10)
docs.text: Ehlers Fisher Transform. Converts price into a Gaussian normal distribution to pinpoint turning points. Returns Struct: fisher, signal.

docs.title: rvi(open, high, low, close, period=10)
docs.text: Relative Vigor Index. Compares bar closing price relative to bar range. Returns Struct: rvi, signal.

docs.title: kst(close)
docs.text: "Know Sure Thing" Oscillator by Martin Pring. Sum of four smoothed rate-of-change indicators. Returns Struct: kst, signal.

docs.title: dpo(close, period=20)
docs.text: Detrended Price Oscillator. Removes longer-term trends to highlight short-term cycles.

docs.title: bop(open, high, low, close)
docs.text: Balance of Market Power: \((Close - Open) / (High - Low)\).

docs.title: cfo(close, period=14)
docs.text: Chande Forecast Oscillator. Percentage difference between actual price and linear regression forecast.

docs.title: squeeze_momentum(high, low, close, bb_period=20, bb_mult=2.0, kc_period=20, kc_mult=1.5, mom_period=None)
docs.text: John Carter's Squeeze Momentum Indicator (popularized by LazyBear). Identifies compression consolidations and explosive breakouts using Bollinger Bands and Keltner Channels, accompanied by an OLS linear regression momentum histogram. Returns Struct: squeeze_on, squeeze_off, no_squeeze, momentum.

docs.title: stc(close, fast_period=23, slow_period=50, cycle_period=10, factor=0.5)
docs.text: Schaff Trend Cycle (STC) Oscillator. Applies a double-smoothed stochastic cycle calculation to a MACD line to identify cyclical turns with reduced lag and fewer false signals.Bounded in \([0, 100]\).

docs.title: Quantitative Statistics & Regression Transforms (12 Indicators)
docs.text: Statistical expressions enable institutional quantitative modeling, factor normalization, and rolling regression without leaving Polars.

docs.title: zscore(close, period=20)
docs.text: Rolling Z-score standardization: \((x - \mu) / \sigma\).

docs.title: percentile_rank(close, period=20)
docs.text: Rolling percentile rank \([0.0, 1.0]\). Indicates what percentage of values in the trailing window were less than or equal to the current bar.

docs.title: skewness(close, period=20)
docs.text: Rolling sample skewness. Measures distribution asymmetry. Executed via pure vectorized polynomial expansion without Python loops.

docs.title: kurtosis(close, period=20)
docs.text: Rolling excess kurtosis. Measures tail risk and probability of extreme moves relative to a normal distribution.

docs.title: rolling_cov(x, y, period=20)
docs.text: Rolling sample covariance between two asset series.

docs.title: rolling_corr(x, y, period=20)
docs.text: Rolling Pearson correlation coefficient \([-1.0, 1.0]\).

docs.title: rolling_beta(asset_returns, benchmark_returns, period=60)
docs.text: Rolling CAPM Market Beta: \(\text{Cov}(R_a, R_b) / \text{Var}(R_b)\). Measures systematic market risk exposure.

docs.title: rolling_alpha(asset_returns, benchmark_returns, rf=0.0, period=60)
docs.text: Rolling Jensen's Alpha: \(\bar{R_a} - (R_f + \beta \cdot (\bar{R_b} - R_f))\). Measures risk-adjusted manager excess return.

docs.title: linear_regression_slope(close, period=14)
docs.text:
Vectorized Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) slope \(\beta_1\). Computed in 0.015 seconds per million rows via closed-form WMA/SMA decomposition:

\[\beta_1 = \frac{6}{N - 1} (\text{WMA} - \text{SMA})\]

docs.title: linear_regression_intercept(close, period=14)
docs.text: Vectorized OLS regression intercept: \(\beta_0 = 4 \cdot \text{SMA} - 3 \cdot \text{WMA}\).

docs.title: linear_regression_angle(close, period=14)
docs.text: Rolling linear regression trend angle in degrees: \(\arctan(\beta_1) \times 180 / \pi\).

docs.title: linear_regression_forecast(close, period=14)
docs.text: Rolling linear regression price forecast for the current bar: \(3 \cdot \text{WMA} - 2 \cdot \text{SMA}\).

docs.title: Trend Indicators & Overlays (28 Indicators)
docs.text: Trend indicators identify the direction and momentum of price movements, smooth market noise, and generate trailing stop and support/resistance levels.

docs.title: sma(close, period=10)
docs.text: Simple Moving Average. Arithmetic mean over a sliding lookback window.

docs.title: ema(close, period=10)
docs.text: Exponential Moving Average. Weights recent prices exponentially higher.

docs.title: wma(close, period=10)
docs.text: Linearly-Weighted Moving Average. Weights linearly increase up to the current bar.

docs.title: hma(close, period=10)
docs.text: Hull Moving Average. Extremely responsive moving average with virtually zero lag.

docs.title: dema(close, period=10)
docs.text: Double Exponential Moving Average: \(2 \cdot \text{EMA} - \text{EMA}(\text{EMA})\).

docs.title: tema(close, period=10)
docs.text: Triple Exponential Moving Average: \(3 \cdot \text{EMA} - 3 \cdot \text{EMA}(\text{EMA}) + \text{EMA}(\text{EMA}(\text{EMA}))\).

docs.title: zlema(close, period=10)
docs.text: Zero-Lag Exponential Moving Average. Uses lagged differences to eliminate lag.

docs.title: t3(close, period=5, vfactor=0.7)
docs.text: Tillson T3 Moving Average. Smooth multi-stage exponential filter.

docs.title: alma(close, period=9, offset=0.85, sigma=6.0)
docs.text: Arnaud Legoux Moving Average. Gaussian-distribution weighted moving average.

docs.title: kama(close, period=10, fast_span=2, slow_span=30)
docs.text: Kaufman's Adaptive Moving Average. Dynamically adjusts smoothing based on the Efficiency Ratio (market volatility).

docs.title: mcginley_dynamic(close, period=14, k=0.6)
docs.text: McGinley Dynamic Average. Self-adjusting tracking indicator designed to prevent whipsaws.

docs.title: vidya(close, period=9, cmo_period=9)
docs.text: Variable Index Dynamic Average (Chande's VIDYA). Scales EMA smoothing by the Chande Momentum Oscillator.

docs.title: adx(high, low, close, period=14)
docs.text: Average Directional Movement Index. Returns Struct: adx, plus_di, minus_di.

docs.title: vortex(high, low, close, period=14)
docs.text: Vortex Indicator. Returns Struct: vi_plus, vi_minus.

docs.title: aroon(high, low, period=25)
docs.text: Aroon Indicator & Oscillator. Returns Struct: up, down, oscillator.

docs.title: chop(high, low, close, period=14)
docs.text: Choppiness Index. Quantifies whether the market is trending (\(< 38.2\)) or consolidating (\(> 61.8\)).

docs.title: mass_index(high, low, fast_period=9, slow_period=25)
docs.text: Mass Index. Predicts trend reversals by analyzing the expansion and contraction of price range.

docs.title: supertrend(high, low, close, period=10, multiplier=3.0)
docs.text: SuperTrend Volatility Stop. Returns Struct: supertrend, direction (\(1\) for bull, \(-1\) for bear).

docs.title: psar(high, low, af_step=0.02, af_max=0.2)
docs.text: Parabolic Stop and Reverse (Trailing SAR).

docs.title: ssl_channel(high, low, close, period=10)
docs.text: SSL Channel (Securement Stop Loss Channel). Returns Struct: ssl_up, ssl_down, hlv (\(1\) for bull, \(-1\) for bear).

docs.title: trend_intensity_index(close, period=30, signal_period=None)
docs.text: Trend Intensity Index (TII) by M.H. Pee. Computes percentage of price deviations above moving average versus total deviations. Returns Struct: tii, signal.

docs.title: center_of_gravity(close, period=10)
docs.text: John Ehlers' Center of Gravity Oscillator. Detects cycle turning points with zero lag.

docs.title: ichimoku(high, low, close, tenkan=9, kijun=26, senkou_b=52, displacement=26)
docs.text: Ichimoku Kinko Hyo Cloud. Returns Struct: tenkan_sen, kijun_sen, senkou_span_a, senkou_span_b, chikou_span.

docs.title: pivot_points(high, low, close)
docs.text: Standard Floor Trader Pivot Points. Returns Struct: pivot, r1, s1, r2, s2, r3, s3.

docs.title: fibonacci_pivots(high, low, close)
docs.text: Fibonacci Pivot Points (38.2%, 61.8%, 100% ratios). Returns Struct: pivot, r1-r3, s1-s3.

docs.title: camarilla_pivots(high, low, close)
docs.text: Camarilla Intraday Pivot Points (8 tight levels). Returns Struct: r1-r4, s1-s4.

docs.title: woodie_pivots(open, high, low, close)
docs.text: Woodie's Pivot Points. Weights closing price more heavily: \((H + L + 2C) / 4\). Returns Struct: pivot, r1, s1, r2, s2.

docs.title: heikin_ashi(open, high, low, close)
docs.text: Heikin-Ashi Candlestick Transform. Computes synthetic smoothed OHLC bars natively without Python loops by formulating \(\text{HA\_Open}_t = 0.5 \cdot \text{HA\_Open}_{t-1} + 0.5 \cdot \text{HA\_Close}_{t-1}\) as an exact \(\text{EMA}(\alpha=0.5)\). Returns Struct: ha_open, ha_high, ha_low, ha_close.

docs.title: Volatility Indicators & Channels (18 Indicators)
docs.text: Volatility indicators measure the dispersion of returns, price range expansion, and channel boundaries.

docs.title: true_range(high, low, close)
docs.text: True Range: \(\max(H - L, |H - C_{prev}|, |L - C_{prev}|)\).

docs.title: atr(high, low, close, period=14)
docs.text: Average True Range using Wilder's smoothing. Measures absolute market volatility.

docs.title: natr(high, low, close, period=14)
docs.text: Normalized Average True Range: \(\text{ATR} / \text{Close} \times 100\). Allows cross-asset volatility comparison.

docs.title: bollinger_bands(close, period=20, num_std=2.0)
docs.text: Bollinger Bands. Returns Struct: upper, middle, lower, bandwidth, percent_b.

docs.title: bollinger_delta(close, period=20, num_std=2.0)
docs.text: Bollinger Band Spread: \(2 \cdot k \cdot \sigma\).

docs.title: keltner_channels(high, low, close, ema=20, atr=10, multiplier=2.0)
docs.text: Keltner Channels. Combines an EMA baseline with ATR-based bands. Returns Struct: upper, middle, lower.

docs.title: keltner_width(high, low, close, ema=20, atr=10, multiplier=2.0)
docs.text: Normalized Keltner Channel Width (%) for Bollinger/Keltner volatility squeeze detection.

docs.title: donchian_channels(high, low, period=20)
docs.text: Donchian Channels. High/Low range breakout channel. Returns Struct: upper, middle, lower.

docs.title: donchian_width(high, low, period=20)
docs.text: Donchian Channel Bandwidth (percentage spread relative to midline).

docs.title: envelopes(close, period=20, percentage=0.025)
docs.text: Moving Average Envelopes. Fixed-percentage bands above and below an SMA midline. Returns Struct: upper, middle, lower.

docs.title: starc_bands(high, low, close, period=20, atr_period=15, multiplier=2.0)
docs.text: STARC Bands (Stoller Average Range Channels). SMA midline + ATR bands. Returns Struct: upper, middle, lower.

docs.title: stddev(close, period=20)
docs.text: Rolling sample standard deviation.

docs.title: ulcer_index(close, period=14)
docs.text: Ulcer Index. Quantifies downside risk and retracement depth.

docs.title: chandelier_exit(high, low, close, period=22, multiplier=3.0)
docs.text: Chandelier Exit. Trailing stop based on highest high/lowest low minus ATR multiple. Returns Struct: long_stop, short_stop.

docs.title: historical_volatility(close, period=20, trading_days=252)
docs.text: Annualized Log Historical Volatility (\(\sigma_{annual}\)).

docs.title: parkinson_volatility(high, low, period=20, trading_days=252)
docs.text: Parkinson Extreme-Value Volatility. 5x more efficient than close-to-close volatility by incorporating intraday High/Low.

docs.title: garman_klass_volatility(open, high, low, close, period=20, trading_days=252)
docs.text: Garman-Klass Efficient Volatility. Incorporates Open, High, Low, and Close for maximum estimator efficiency (8x better than close-to-close).

docs.title: chaikin_volatility(high, low, period=10, roc_period=10)
docs.text: Chaikin Volatility. Percentage rate of change of the exponential moving average of the High-Low spread.

docs.title: Volume Indicators (15 Indicators)
docs.text: Volume indicators evaluate institutional buying and selling pressure, money flow, and volume-price divergence.

docs.title: obv(close, volume)
docs.text: On-Balance Volume. Cumulative volume added on up bars and subtracted on down bars.

docs.title: vwap(high, low, close, volume, period=None)
docs.text: Volume Weighted Average Price. Computes cumulative VWAP (default) or rolling VWAP when period is specified.

docs.title: vwap_bands(high, low, close, volume, period=None, mult1=1.0, mult2=2.0, mult3=3.0)
docs.text: Volume Weighted Average Price with Standard Deviation Bands. Returns Struct: vwap, upper_1, lower_1, upper_2, lower_2, upper_3, lower_3.

docs.title: vwma(close, volume, period=20)
docs.text: Volume Weighted Moving Average. Moving average weighted by bar volume.

docs.title: cmf(high, low, close, volume, period=20)
docs.text: Chaikin Money Flow. Quantifies money accumulation and distribution over a lookback window.

docs.title: adl(high, low, close, volume)
docs.text: Accumulation/Distribution Line. Cumulative volume based on the Close Location Value (CLV).

docs.title: mfi(high, low, close, volume, period=14)
docs.text: Money Flow Index. Volume-weighted RSI bounded between 0 and 100.

docs.title: eom(high, low, volume, period=14)
docs.text: Ease of Movement (EMV). Relates price change to trading volume.

docs.title: klinger(high, low, close, volume, fast=34, slow=55, signal=13)
docs.text: Klinger Volume Oscillator. Determines long-term money flow while remaining sensitive to short-term fluctuations. Returns Struct: klinger, signal.

docs.title: nvi(close, volume, initial=1000.0)
docs.text: Negative Volume Index. Follows smart money by updating only when volume decreases.

docs.title: pvi(close, volume, initial=1000.0)
docs.text: Positive Volume Index. Follows retail crowd activity by updating only when volume increases.

docs.title: pvt(close, volume)
docs.text: Price Volume Trend. Cumulative volume scaled by percentage price changes.

docs.title: force_index(close, volume, period=13)
docs.text: Elder's Force Index (EFI). Measures the raw price and volume force behind market moves.

docs.title: vpci(close, volume, period_short=5, period_long=25)
docs.text: Volume Price Confirmation Indicator. Compares price-weighted volume against volume-weighted price.

docs.title: vr(close, volume, period=26)
docs.text: Volume Ratio. Ratio of volume on rising bars vs volume on falling bars.
